x: It was very pleasing to see 'new boy' Norman Stairs in his first distance race for us, running so well. More than anything experience plays a great part in this race.

When Len Bishop our next scorer arrived we were last of the four, but the very next man to arrive in was find-of-the-season N. Stairs whose effort took us to a narrow team win—four points covering the first four teams.
…for his 6th place in the Kent '20' (1 : 55 : 44) and his 9th in the Chichester to Portsmouth '16' (1 : 33 : 45); and to Norman Stairs, who runs only in the summer, for his winning of the "A.…
Also, Ron Linstead on his magnificent run in the I.O.M. 37¾ (what a pity we had no "third man"!), and Norman Stairs our new Club marathon champion, who hails all the way from Aldershot.
Belgrave were without Sawyer and Linstead, but Denis Jones ran very well and with the support of Norman Stairs and Len Bishop, we were placed third.

It was very encouraging to see John Moore once again out on the road and approaching something like his old fitness. Also out that day were Norman Stairs, Ray Conway,and Charlie Manning. We congratulate all concerned on a profitable Bank Holiday's running.

Norman Stairs finished 18th in the R.R.C. marathon on July 13th. His time of 2:47:04 was 19:03 behind Lusty of Ealing---the surprise winner.

From left to right, Norman Stairs, Barry Sawyer, Alan Bishop, Len Bishop, John Moore, Charlie Walker, Denis Jones, and Derek Crookes. This picture was taken at Windsor Castle just before they were sent on their way by Her Majesty The Queen.

A "ghost" Belgrave team ran in the Wimbledon '10' on the day of the Southern London-Brighton relay and finished 10th. Jack Brown was 27th in 55:18 Norman Stairs 36th in 56:17, Pete Sadler 38th in 56:23 and Bob Glover 46th in 57:12.
Norman Stairs & Wally Wortley carried our colours thro' South London at the head of the field, but the latter soon eased leaving Norman a minute clear at Croydon.
In the Redhill and Reigate '10¾' on March 30th, Arthur Bruce (59:26) was 16th and Norman Stairs (59:29) 17th.
Wally led at 5 miles but was overtaken by our own Norman Stairs who went way ahead to lead by 3½ minutes at'20'. Stairs then hit a bad patch and was passed at 25 miles - 5miles later he retired.

Norman Stairs had a fine day's outing over the hilly Isle of Wight course last May 23rd. He was 4th in the scratch event,1st in the Hampshire County Championship,1st in the handicap and led our team to 2nd place in the team contest.

John Moore and Norman Stairs had been backing up well and they finished strongly in 22nd and 24th positions with personal best times. Charlie Walker completed our scoring three,but with a time of 5mins slower than last year.

However,both our leading runners weakened in the final stages,and although Pat hung on to his second place (a fine effort) John was pushed back to 10th. Belgrave regained the team title from Notts AC,thanks to a good supporting run by Norman Stairs.

On the same day as the Southall'10',Norman Stairs and Alan Bishop ran in the SLH'30' at Coulsdon.Norman was 7th at the marathon distance in 2:51:20 but the oppresive conditions forced him to call it a day- Alan completed the "additional" 4 miles to finish 24th in 4:02:08.

Last year Norman Stairs forced the pace early on, opened up a big lead, then blew up.Although he struggled on gamely to finish 7th it was quite apparent that he was capable of better things if his pace judgement improved.
Norman Stairs ran a sound race to finish 39th and John Moore,still striving to get fit after his recent illness,completed our scoring 'A' team in 54th place.
